title: All four ‘Lord of the Rings’ movie Hobbits explored Boston together this weekend
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Sean Astin, Elijah Wood, Dominic Monaghan, and Billy Boyd reunited in Boston during Fan Expo Boston.
The actors visited La Royal Cambridge, a Peruvian restaurant, and found time for Boston's Green Dragon pub.
The reunion celebrated 25 years of the 'Lord of the Rings' series, featuring an event at Fan Expo Boston.

title: Jaylen Brown to host free Boston block party at Boston Common on Aug. 30
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Jaylen Brown will host '741 Frequency Fest' at Boston Common on August 30 from 2 to 7 p.m.
The event features music, games, giveaways, and a concert, celebrating Brown's decade with the Celtics.
Brown was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers after ten seasons and five All-Star selections with Boston.

title: Patriots reportedly releasing 2024 third-round pick Caedan Wallace
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: The Patriots are reportedly releasing offensive guard Caedan Wallace, a 2024 third-round pick from Penn State.
Wallace, 26, played 10 games over two seasons, with limited snaps in 2025 after an active 2024 season.
Releasing Wallace leaves only Drake Maye and Marcellas Dial Jr. from the Patriots' 2024 draft class on the roster.

title: Comedian Matt Rife throws down with a paranormal investigator over ‘haunted’ event in Salem
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Comedian Matt Rife told paranormal investigator Chris Mac to 'remove yourself from this earth' in a deleted online comment.
Rife and ghost hunter Elton Castee plan to exhibit the Warren Museum's haunted items in Salem on Aug. 27.
Supporters criticized Rife's comments about Mac, who is autistic, calling them bullying and disgraceful.

title: Hunter Henry agrees to a two-year extension with the Patriots
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Hunter Henry, 31, signs a two-year extension with the Patriots worth up to $20 million.
The contract includes $14.5 million guaranteed money and a $4.2 million signing bonus.
Henry has 259 catches and 26 touchdowns since joining the Patriots in 2021.

title: 83-year-old drives Jaguar into Acton CVS, causing major damage
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: An 83-year-old woman crashed her Jaguar into a CVS in Acton, causing significant interior damage.
Neither the 83-year-old driver nor her 88-year-old passenger were injured in the crash.
The CVS will stay closed for repairs, and the crash is under investigation by Acton Police.

title: Logan runway closure this fall could mean more flight delays
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Logan Airport will close Runway 27 for a 75-day safety project starting August 31, impacting flight operations.
The project includes installing an Engineered Material Arresting System (EMAS) to prevent runway overruns.
Nearby communities will experience increased air traffic and construction noise during the runway closure.

title: One dead, 3 injured in head-on crash on the Cape
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A head-on crash in Sandwich on Sunday involved a 2011 Toyota Prius and a 2017 Toyota RAV4.
The male driver of the Prius died after being transported to Cape Cod Hospital; three RAV4 occupants were injured.
The crash occurred at around 8:50 p.m. on Farmersville Road; the cause remains under investigation.

title: Driver on South Shore narrowly escaped before commuter train totaled his Camry
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 2016 Toyota Camry was struck by a Commuter Rail train on the Greenbush Line in Cohasset, South Shore.
The driver, a 33-year-old Mansfield man, made a wrong turn onto the tracks but exited safely before the collision.
No injuries were reported among the 15 passengers on the train or the crew; North Main Street was closed for two hours.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues with psychiatrist under cross-examination
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy's murder trial continues as psychiatrist Dr. Jennifer Tufts testifies under cross-examination.
Dr. Tufts stated Clancy denied suicidal or homicidal thoughts before allegedly killing her three children.
Clancy's insanity defense argues postpartum mental illness and psychiatric medications contributed to her actions.
